talon.name: Plantar fasciopathy
talon.whatYouFeel: Sharp pain under the heel with the first steps in the morning or after sitting, which eases as you walk.
talon.whatHappens: The plantar fascia is a fibrous sheet stretched from the heel to the toes. Its attachment on the heel becomes painful when it is overloaded.
talon.whoIsAffected: People who stand for long periods, runners, excess weight.
talon.warning: Pain at rest or at night, pins and needles in the foot: see a doctor. A runner whose heel hurts when squeezed from the sides: stop running and see a doctor, a stress fracture is possible. Pain in both heels before 45 with a stiff back in the morning: tell your doctor. Child aged 8 to 14: heel pain most often comes from the growth cartilage (Sever's disease), which is managed differently.

hallux.name: Hallux valgus
hallux.whatYouFeel: A bump at the base of the big toe, redness and pain when it rubs in the shoe, big toe drifting towards the others.
hallux.whatHappens: The first metatarsal moves towards the inside of the foot and the big toe angles outwards. The bulge of the joint rubs in the shoe.
hallux.whoIsAffected: More often women, and more and more with age.
hallux.warning: A big toe that suddenly becomes red, hot, swollen and very painful, often at night: see a doctor promptly, it is often an attack of gout. Exercises relieve but do not straighten the toe. Choose shoes that are wide at the front. A wound or redness in a person with diabetes: see a doctor promptly.

entorse.name: Lateral ankle sprain
entorse.whatYouFeel: Pain and swelling on the outer side of the ankle after a twist, sometimes a bruise the next day.
entorse.whatHappens: The foot turns inwards and the ligaments on the outer side are stretched or torn, starting with the anterior talofibular ligament.
entorse.whoIsAffected: Athletes, but also everyday life, on a misstep.
entorse.warning: An X-ray is needed if you cannot take four steps, just after the twist or later, or if the bone hurts when pressing on the back or tip of an ankle bone, the base of the fifth metatarsal (outer edge of the foot) or the navicular bone (inner edge). A hot, red, swollen foot without a real twist in a person with diabetes: see a doctor the same day.

metat.name: Metatarsalgia
metat.commonName: Pain under the front of the foot
metat.whatYouFeel: Pain under the base of the second and third toes, like a stone in the shoe, worse barefoot on a hard floor.
metat.whatHappens: The heads of the middle metatarsals take too much pressure. The joint capsule and the fat pad become irritated.
metat.whoIsAffected: High-arched feet, high heels, bunions, running.
metat.warning: A toe that changes shape or swelling of the forefoot: see a doctor.

rigidus.name: Hallux rigidus
rigidus.whatYouFeel: Pain and stiffness at the base of the big toe as the foot rolls off, a bump on top of the joint.
rigidus.whatHappens: The cartilage of the big toe joint wears and a bone spur forms on top, which blocks upward bending.
rigidus.warning: Shoes with a stiff or rocker sole. A joint that suddenly becomes red, hot and very painful: see a doctor promptly. See a doctor if walking stays limited.

achille.name: Achilles tendinopathy
achille.whatYouFeel: Pain and stiffness at the back of the ankle on getting up and at the start of exercise, a thickened tendon that is tender when pinched.
achille.whatHappens: The Achilles tendon links the calf to the heel. Its middle part, 2 to 6 cm above its attachment on the heel bone, thickens and becomes painful.
achille.whoIsAffected: Runners, jumping sports, returning to sport after 40. The risk rises with some antibiotics (fluoroquinolones) and cortisone.
achille.warning: A sudden snap like a whip crack, unable to rise onto your toes: emergency (112 or your local number). Tendon pain during or after a fluoroquinolone antibiotic (ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, ofloxacin…): stop sport and call your doctor.

morton.name: Morton's neuroma
morton.whatYouFeel: Burning or shooting pain between the third and fourth toes, eased by taking off the shoe and massaging the foot.
morton.whatHappens: The nerve that runs between two metatarsal heads thickens from being compressed.
morton.warning: No improvement with better footwear: see a doctor, insoles or an injection can help.

tibpost.name: Tibialis posterior tendinopathy
tibpost.whatYouFeel: Pain behind and under the inner ankle bone, a flattening arch, difficulty rising onto the toes of one foot.
tibpost.whatHappens: The tibialis posterior tendon wraps around the inner ankle bone and supports the arch of the foot. When it weakens, the foot collapses.
tibpost.whoIsAffected: Women over 40, excess weight, flat feet, runners.
tibpost.warning: An arch collapsing on one side only: see a doctor early, an insole protects the tendon.

instab.name: Chronic ankle instability
instab.whatYouFeel: Repeated sprains, an ankle that gives way on uneven ground, apprehension.
instab.whatHappens: After a sprain, the ligaments can stay stretched and the ankle loses its protective reflexes.
instab.whoIsAffected: After one or more sprains without proper rehabilitation.
instab.warning: Frequent giving way despite three months of rehabilitation: see a doctor.

fibulaires.name: Peroneal (fibularis) tendinopathy
fibulaires.commonName: Pain behind the outer ankle bone
fibulaires.whatYouFeel: Pain behind and under the outer ankle bone, when running and on sloping ground.
fibulaires.whatHappens: The two fibularis (peroneal) tendons wrap around the outer ankle bone and stop the foot from rolling inwards.
fibulaires.whoIsAffected: Runners, high-arched feet, after a sprain.
fibulaires.warning: A snap or a tendon that jumps behind the ankle bone: see a doctor.

fatigue.name: Metatarsal stress fracture
fatigue.commonName: Pain on top of the foot when walking
fatigue.whatYouFeel: Pain on top of the forefoot, pinpointed on a bone, swelling, worse when bearing weight.
fatigue.whatHappens: Tiny cracks build up in the second or third metatarsal when the load increases faster than the bone can adapt.
fatigue.whoIsAffected: Runners, walkers, soldiers, after a sudden increase in activity. More common with inadequate nutrition, absent or irregular periods, or osteoporosis.
fatigue.warning: Stop running and jumping now and see a doctor within the week. The X-ray is often normal at first; an MRI can confirm it. It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks without impact. Pain on the outer edge of the foot (base of the fifth metatarsal) or in the middle of the top of the foot (navicular bone): see a doctor promptly, these fractures heal poorly without treatment.

tarsien.name: Tarsal tunnel syndrome
tarsien.whatYouFeel: Burning and pins and needles under the foot and towards the toes, worse standing and at night.
tarsien.whatHappens: The tibial nerve runs behind the inner ankle bone under a fibrous band, where it can be compressed.
tarsien.whoIsAffected: Flat feet, after an ankle sprain or fracture.
tarsien.warning: Loss of feeling under the foot: see a doctor.

ecart.name: Spread the big toe
ecart.how: Foot flat, move the big toe away from the others without lifting it. Hold 5 s, 10 times.

court.name: Short foot
court.how: Sitting, draw the front of the foot towards the heel without curling the toes. Hold 5 s, 10 times.

mobgo.name: Big toe mobilisation
mobgo.how: Hold the big toe and move it gently up and down. 10 times, without forcing.

etapo.name: Plantar fascia stretch
etapo.how: Sitting, foot on the opposite knee, pull the toes towards the shin. 10 times 10 s, before your first steps.

rath.name: Heel raises with toes on a towel
rath.how: On a step, rise over 3 s, hold 2 s, lower over 3 s. 3 sets of 12, every other day.
rath.videoSearch: plantar fasciitis strengthening heel raise towel

etmol.name: Calf stretch
etmol.how: Hands on the wall, back leg straight, heel on the floor. 3 times 30 s.

alpha.name: Ankle alphabet
alpha.how: From the first days, draw the letters with the tip of the foot. Twice a day. In the first days: protect without immobilising, raise the leg, avoid anti-inflammatories, then get moving again as pain allows.

equi.name: Single-leg balance
equi.how: Once you can bear weight, 3 times 30 s, then with eyes closed or on a cushion.

pointes.name: Heel raises
pointes.how: On both feet then on one, lowering slowly. 3 sets of 12.

alfred.name: Slow heel drop on a step
alfred.how: Rise on both feet, lower over 3 s on the painful foot. 3 sets of 15, once or twice a day. If the pain is at the attachment on the heel, lower only to the level of the step, not below.

isoach.name: Heel raise hold
isoach.how: On both feet, hold at the top for 30 to 45 s. 5 holds.

ever.name: Eversion with a band
ever.how: Foot outwards against the band, return slowly. 3 sets of 15.

inver.name: Inversion with a band
inver.how: Foot inwards against the band, return slowly. 3 sets of 15.
inver.videoSearch: ankle inversion band tibialis posterior strengthening

serv.name: Towel scrunches
serv.how: Scrunch the towel towards you with your toes. 3 times 1 minute.

chaus.name: Wide shoes and insole
chaus.how: Wide forefoot, low heel, insole with support just behind the metatarsal heads.

decharge.name: Limited walking and protected weight-bearing
decharge.how: Cut down walking and stop running as long as bearing weight hurts.

velo.name: Cycling or swimming
velo.how: Keep fit without impact, 20 to 30 minutes, 3 times a week.
velo.videoSearch: low impact exercise foot injury cycling swimming

nerf.name: Tibial nerve glide
nerf.how: Sitting, leg straight, pull the toes up then release. 10 times slowly.

saut.name: Hops and dynamic landings
saut.how: Small hops on the spot, then from one foot to the other, at the end of rehabilitation.
